From the Oyez page for Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka (1) (https://www.oyez.org/cases/1940-1955/347us483), the recorded information is as follows:

- Docket number: 1
- Deciding Court: Warren Court
- Argued dates: December 9–11, 1952
- Reargued dates: December 7–9, 1953
- Decided date: May 17, 1954

Question (from the Question section on the Brown I page):
- "Does the segregation of public education based solely on race violate the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment?"

Decision information (from the Conclusion decision card on the Brown I page):
- Decision split: Unanimous decision
- Prevailing side: for Brown et al.
- Majority-opinion author: Earl Warren ("majority opinion by Earl Warren")
- One-line holding (the single-sentence holding immediately below the majority-opinion label on the Conclusion card, not the longer explanatory paragraph):
  - "Separate but equal educational facilities for racial minorities is inherently unequal violating the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment."
